description:
Castello di San Fabiano is in fact a small historic hamlet in the Crete Senesi region, just 12 km from Siena, between the Chianti and the Val d'Orcia. The complex is made up of a 12th-century tower, the manor villa, farm buildings, and a church built in the year 867 dedicated to San Fabiano. The San Fabiano tower was part of a system of watchtowers along the Via Francigena, the medieval pilgrimage route to Rome.

The complex was restored in 1950 by the Fiorentini family, who transformed the old watchtower and its farm outbuildings into a historic residence. Today guests are personally welcomed by the owners, in a setting of three hectares of parkland divided into distinct gardens.

The 867 AD church predates most of the structures found across this collection by several centuries, giving San Fabiano one of the oldest confirmed dates of any element in the Italy castle-hotel list.

The tower's role within the Via Francigena's watchtower network ties San Fabiano to the same medieval pilgrimage infrastructure connected to properties like Castel Pietraio elsewhere in this collection, part of a broader chain of fortified points along the route to Rome.

The Fiorentini family's personal, hands-on hospitality since 1950 gives San Fabiano a genuinely small-scale, family-run character distinct from the more corporately managed resort properties in this collection.

The surrounding Crete Senesi, with its distinctive clay hills, gives guests staying at San Fabiano access to one of Tuscany's most visually striking and least crowded landscapes, between Siena and the Val d'Orcia.
history: San Fabiano is a small historic hamlet in the Crete Senesi, comprising a 12th-century watchtower once part of the Via Francigena's defensive system, a manor villa, farm buildings, and a church dating to 867 AD. Restored in 1950 by the Fiorentini family, the complex today combines accommodation across the manor villa and a nearby casale, with guests personally welcomed by the owners.

faqs.question: Is San Fabiano a conventional hotel?
faqs.answer: Not technically — it's a family-run historic residence, with personal hospitality from the owners, but without all the standard services of a conventional hotel (such as 24-hour reception).

faqs.question: How old is the church at San Fabiano?
faqs.answer: It dates to the year 867 AD, dedicated to San Fabiano, making it one of the oldest elements on the property.

faqs.question: Are all the accommodations at San Fabiano within one building?
faqs.answer: No — up to 30 beds are split between the manor villa (including 6 suites on its second floor) and a separate casale (farmhouse) on the estate.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** About 15 minutes from Monteroni d'Arbia and 25 minutes from Siena by car; Florence's Peretola Airport (FLR) is about 1h15.

**Rooms & rates:** Up to 30 beds among rooms, suites and apartments, split between the manor villa (including 6 suites on the second floor) and the estate's casale (farmhouse).

**On-site:** Historic church dating to 867 AD, 3-hectare park with gardens, organic breakfast, wedding space.

**Good to know:** This is not technically a "hotel" but a family-run historic residence — personal service, but without all the standard amenities of a conventional hotel (24-hour reception, etc.).

**Combine with:** Siena (~25 min), Montepulciano and Pienza (~1h), Florence and Arezzo (~1h in either direction).
